question: What are the disadvantages of Test-Driven Development (TDD)?
answerGeneral: TDD's main disadvantages: it slows down initial development speed (writing tests first takes discipline and time), it requires upfront design clarity that isn't always available, it can lead to over-mocking when tests drive implementation too closely, and it doesn't work well for UI/exploratory code where you don't know the contract until you've built it. TDD also becomes painful when requirements change frequently, since tests must be rewritten alongside the implementation. It also requires team-wide buy-in — partial adoption leads to inconsistency. That said, in well-understood domains with stable requirements, TDD's benefits (better design, built-in regression net) usually outweigh the costs.
answerGeneralTr: TDD'nin başlıca dezavantajları: başlangıçtaki geliştirme hızını yavaşlatır (önce test yazmak disiplin ve zaman gerektirir), testler uygulamayı çok yakından yönlendirdiğinde aşırı mock'lamaya yol açabilir, ve sözleşmeyi inşa edene kadar bilmediğiniz UI/keşifsel kodlarda iyi çalışmaz. TDD ayrıca gereksinimler sık sık değiştiğinde de zahmetli hale gelir; çünkü testlerin uygulamayla birlikte yeniden yazılması gerekir. Aynı zamanda ekip genelinde benimseme gerektirir — kısmi benimseme tutarsızlığa yol açar. Bununla birlikte, kararlı gereksinimlere sahip iyi anlaşılmış alanlarda TDD'nin faydaları (daha iyi tasarım, yerleşik regresyon ağı) genellikle maliyetleri aşar.
detailMd:
## Disadvantages of TDD

## 1. Slower Initial Velocity

Writing tests before code is a discipline shift. Early in a project or feature, the cost is felt immediately — the benefit (fewer bugs, easier refactoring) comes later.

```
TDD workflow:
  Red → Green → Refactor (× every function)

With TDD: more keystrokes upfront
Without TDD: faster now, slower later (debugging, regression)
```

## 2. Requires Upfront Design Clarity

TDD works best when you know what the API should look like before you build it. Exploratory work is hard to TDD:

```typescript
// Hard to TDD: you don't know the shape yet
// "Build me a drag-and-drop interface" → unclear API until you prototype

// Easy to TDD: clear contract
test('calculateTax returns 0 for zero income', () => {
  expect(calculateTax(0)).toBe(0);
});
```

## 3. Test Maintenance Overhead

When requirements change, tests must change first — then the implementation. In fast-moving codebases, this doubles the cost of every requirements change:

```
Requirement change → update tests → update implementation → verify
```

## 4. Over-Mocking Temptation

TDD can push you toward highly isolated unit tests that mock everything — creating a test suite that passes while the real system fails:

```typescript
// TDD'd in isolation, broken in reality
jest.mock('./paymentGateway');
jest.mock('./emailService');
jest.mock('./inventoryService');
// All green — but the actual integrations are never tested
```

## 5. Doesn't Suit All Problem Types

```
✅ TDD excels at:
   - Business logic (calculators, validators, transformers)
   - API/service layer design
   - Bug-driven development (write failing test for bug first)

❌ TDD struggles with:
   - UI prototyping (changing layouts constantly)
   - ML/AI (non-deterministic outputs)
   - Legacy code with no seams (hard to write tests before refactoring)
   - Spike/discovery work
```

## 6. Team Adoption Cost

TDD requires a team-wide cultural shift. A team that does TDD inconsistently often ends up worse than one that doesn't do it at all — patchy test suites with no shared discipline.

## The Balanced View

```
Use TDD for: business logic, service layers, utility functions
Skip TDD for: UI exploration, spikes, integrations you'll test with E2E
Always do: write tests before fixing bugs (at minimum)
```

question: How do you design a testing strategy for code that relies on caching?
answerGeneral: Cache testing requires controlling cache state explicitly. The strategy: (1) test cache-miss paths by starting with an empty/cleared cache, (2) test cache-hit paths by pre-populating the cache before calling the function, (3) test TTL behaviour using fake timers (jest.useFakeTimers), (4) test cache invalidation by verifying stale entries are removed after the invalidation trigger. Abstract the cache behind an interface so you can use an in-memory fake in unit tests and the real Redis/LRU cache in integration tests.
answerGeneralTr: Cache testleri, cache durumunu açıkça kontrol etmeyi gerektirir. Strateji: (1) boş/temizlenmiş bir cache ile başlayarak cache-miss yollarını test edin, (2) fonksiyonu çağırmadan önce cache'i önceden doldurarak cache-hit yollarını test edin, (3) sahte zamanlayıcılar kullanarak TTL davranışını test edin (jest.useFakeTimers), (4) invalidasyon tetikleyicisinden sonra eski girdilerin kaldırıldığını doğrulayarak cache invalidasyonunu test edin. Birim testlerinde bellek içi sahte, entegrasyon testlerinde gerçek Redis/LRU cache kullanabilmek için cache'i bir arayüzün arkasına soyutlayın.
